critique: This run shows why assertions 2 and 3 are the discriminating ones: the measuring is careful and the CSS recommendations are arguably more detailed than the with-skill run's, yet the headline numbers are fuzz-% diffs against a noisy AI raster for BOTH the surface and the app, so the user cannot tell tolerance from drift. Assertion 1 as worded lets this run pass by importing the identical token sheet even though global.css's layout rules are not shared — tighten it to name global.css. Assertion 2 conflates two things (shooting the live URL, and producing report.json); when the URL genuinely cannot render the state, the eval should say what a correct outcome looks like (an 'inconclusive' gate with the reason) instead of leaving an honest blocker indistinguishable from not trying. Assertion 5 is not gradable without a transcript or per-round artifacts. Uncovered outcomes worth an assertion: the match surface contains raw hex colours (tokens-only discipline), and the coordinate frame of the reported deltas (1586-frame page px here vs logical px) — the prompt says 'in pixels' and the two runs answered in different frames.
